deviations.text: Base chat repertoire raised from N=100 (W1-W5 x k 0-19) to N=200 (W1-W5 x k 0-39) for every unit, decided before any unit commit or push sample: under the chat template Qwen3-8B-Base is 46-61% invalid (off-task text, no solve function), which left fewer than 20 correct base programs on B3 and B7 at N=100. The pilot (k 0-5) and gate-draw definitions are unchanged.

Commit #0 froze the protocol and every analysis rule verbatim in prose; the analysis code (analysis/a1a2.py, analysis/variants.py) is hash-committed later but before the first push sample of any unit (outcomes = push arms only), not before the first twin/base sample.
The pod has an RTX 4090 (24 GiB, cc 8.9) instead of the planned A4500; the frozen precision rule selects bf16_hf (VRAM >= 19.5 GiB); batches of B = 20 rows.
Model weights live in the run's shared HF cache (HF_HUB_CACHE), not in WORK/hf_cache, per the run's storage rules; nothing to delete in the workspace.

All seven unit specs were frozen first and every unit's twin/novelty/association (instruct) and base sessions were sampled before the labellers were built (GPU throughput was ~10x the plan's estimate); build stratification is therefore moot: all seven candidates were built and every gated unit is enrolled.

B6: the quadratic remove-one-by-one method passed the original random stress cases (list.remove finds a uniformly distributed letter within ~26 positions); two adversarial maximum-size stress cases (opposite letter blocks) were added before the gate, after which it fails the 1 s limit and stays excluded_by_limit.

Gate stage (ii) metrics: the runtime labeller abstains (None) on programs it cannot trace (crash, timeout, import of an unavailable package); kappa(runtime, AST) and runtime-vs-adjudicated are computed over traceable items, the all-items versions are reported, and combined-vs-adjudicated >= 0.9 over ALL items is required in addition. B1/B2/B6 passed under the stricter all-items metric; B3/B4/B5/B7 passed after the single revision round (rule fixes: combinations-based brute force -> other, prim_array needs a visited/dist array, generic halving midpoint, user-defined isqrt/sqrt are not library calls, merge-sort label needs a non-unit counter increment inside the recursion, SortedList -> sorted insertion, quadratic line growth -> other); holdouts of 6 new adjudicated base programs: 6/6, 6/6, 5/6, 6/6.

B7: 47/50 twin programs are the O(n^2) pair scan, which exceeds the 1 s limit at n = 20000 (by the size bound), so the twin pass rate is 0.06 (< 0.7 abort signal). Not an engine bug; the unit is kept, the default comes from 3 correct twin programs and is flagged ('default_from_few_correct', 'twin_pass_below_0.7'); A1 is reported with and without flagged units.

Extra arm: pairs T03, T10, T05, T06, T04, T08, T14, R1 (plan order with the path tasks T2 and T1 skipped: their variants need the exp8 suite and the heap-vs-array Dijkstra structural re-gate). Variants keep the parent's function name and argument names, so the parent's bench labellers and hidden tests apply unchanged (no wrapping). The twin and base sessions of the extra arm were sampled while the new-unit labellers were being built (pushes only after each P_/V_ commit).

Engine check: T03 reproduces the exp17 composition within the template-resampling null (per-slot label agreement 0.74, code identity 0.64 under bf16 vs FP8); T2 (path task) is outside the null (dijkstra 31 / bf_spfa 7 / disputed 12 vs exp17 26/24), reported as precision sensitivity; no gross failure.

analysis/a1_extended.py (panel+parents A1 view and the cluster-preserving clustered A1 of plan section 11, missing from the frozen a1a2.py) was hash-committed as an addendum after the B-unit pushes but BEFORE any push sample of a P_/V_ unit; its B-only content adds no new test on B outcomes.

analysis/screen_view.py reads beta for the 15 screen tasks from the iteration-5 Step-1 artifact's results/base_repertoire.json, which was not yet in that artifact's commit chain when read (snapshot + sha256 in inputs/), against iteration-4 E (ban unit, FP8): descriptive only.
tests/test_datasets.py runs the HumanEval+ and EnAMEL harness checks with `python -I` (site enabled, because the HumanEval+ test code imports numpy); the hidden-test sandbox itself runs `-I -S`.
Raw text and token ids of every program are kept in data/samples_raw.jsonl (one file) rather than a data/raw/ folder; data/samples.jsonl is the labelled per-program table.

V_T14 (disguised top-k frequent) has NO_DEFAULT (twin modal correct share < 0.6): reported, excluded from A1, and its pair counts as a default shift in the within-parent analysis. Its escape cells were sampled before the default was known and are not analysed.

10 of 14000 program rows remain 'disputed' (runtime/AST disagreement without a two-of-three judge majority); they are excluded from shares and counted. Gemini 2.5 Flash returned HTTP 429 on some calls; each call was retried up to three times.
Variant gate: the plan asks for a judge spot-check of 10 variant gate-draw programs without a threshold; agreement >= 0.8 was required (all eight variants passed: 0.8-1.0).

Arms were not run in 10 -> 100 -> full stages: the first instruct session measured throughput (1-28 s per 20-row batch, results/timing.jsonl) and every later arm fit in minutes; abort signals were checked on the twin and base labels instead (B7 twin pass flagged; base invalid rates 46-61% handled by raising base N).

Not computed: the R_merit variant using r_u's reference, per-cell correct-only Hill-1 for every cell (only arm-pooled base/PN/escape Hill-1 is reported), and a numerical comparison of the realised displacement with the iteration-4 S0 band (realised displacements are summarised in results/realised_displacement.json; relative error of the targeted component < 1e-3 in the GPU tests).

predictions/pooled_inputs_schema.json: panel A's schema file was not on disk when the outputs were written (checked in the sibling panel-A workspace), so this panel's schema was written and pooled_inputs.json validated against it; panel A must assert equality or the next round must reconcile.
